title: Soybean Hairy Root Transformation for the Analysis of Gene Function
protocol: Place 16-20 round Williams 82 soybean seeds in a 50 mL centrifuge tube.
Add 30 mL of 70% isopropyl alcohol, gently shake for 30 s, and then decant the alcohol.
Gently shake the seeds with 30 mL of 10% bleach for 10 s and allow the seeds to sit in the solution for 5 min at room temperature (25 °C).
Drain the bleach.
Repeat the shaking three times with 30 mL of sterile ultrapure H2O for 1 min per rinse, discarding water between each rinse.
Place sterilized seeds on filter paper saturated with 5 mL of germination and co-cultivation medium in sterile Petri dishes.
Place plates in the dark at room temperature (25 °C) for 3 days.
Transfer plates to 22 °C under 16 h cool-white T5 fluorescent lights (100 µE m-2·s-1) for 4 days.
Reconstitute pGWB series vectors.
Transform a binary vector harboring the gene of interest into A. rhizogenes pRi2659 using electroporation.
Design primers to detect the Ti plasmid gene VirD2 (forward: 5'-CCCGATCGAGCTCAAGTTAT-3', reverse: 5'-TCGTCTGGCTGACTTTCGT-3').
Test Agrobacterium colonies for the retention of VirD2 by PCR using a PCR Kit.
Select an A. rhizogenes colony containing both VirD2 and the gene of interest (GOI).
Streak out selected A. rhizogenes colony onto LB medium plates with appropriate antibiotics (50 mg/L) and incubate overnight at 30 °C.
If using spectinomycin, add a concentration of 100 mg/L to the LB medium plates.
Scrape off approximately 1.5 cm length of K599 Agrobacterium from the LB plates using a P200 pipette tip.
Resuspend the scraped cells in 1 mL of phosphate buffer (PB; 0.01 M Na2HPO4, 0.15 M NaCl, pH 7.5).
Dilute Agrobacterium in sterilized, ultrapure H2O (v/v = 1:1) and acetosyringone (AS; v/v = 1:1000).
Measure the absorbance using a cuvette tube at an optical density of 600 nm (OD600). The expected optimal range is between 0.5 and 0.8.
Dip a sterilized scalpel in the K599 Agrobacterium solution.
Make several 1 mm deep cuts along the inner surface (adaxial, flat side) of the cotyledon using the dipped scalpel.
Stabilize the cotyledon with sterilized forceps during inoculation.
Place about 6-8 cotyledons cut side-down on a Petri dish containing filter paper saturated with GC medium and acetosyringone (AS).
Transfer the infected cotyledons to hairy root growth (HRG) plates prepared with half-strength MS, 3% sucrose (pH = 5.8), and 2.6 g/L Gelzan.
Add 2.5 mL/L vitamins mixture and 500 mg/L timentin to the HRG medium after autoclaving.
Incubate the plates at room temperature (25 °C) for 3 days under a 16 h photoperiod (~65 µE).
Transfer the infected cotyledons from GC medium plates to HRG plates prepared in taller Petri dish plates (100 mm x 25 mm).
Incubate the HRG plates at 22 °C in a growth chamber with parameters set to 100 µE light on a 16 h photoperiod until primary roots with secondary roots of 2-3 cm length are observed (~3-4 weeks).
Harvest primary roots (5-7 cm in length) containing secondary roots (2-3 cm in length).
Transfer harvested roots to selection HRG plates containing appropriate antibiotics.
Let the harvest roots grow for 5 more days on the selection HRG plates.
Harvest transgenic HRs with secondary roots 3-6 cm in length after day 5.
Cut the secondary roots into 1 cm pieces if performing elicitor or chemical treatments.
Place approximately 100 mg of root pieces on HRG agar in a pile for treatment.
Saturate the piles with 80 μL of the appropriate treatment and allow to incubate at RT (25 °C).
Proceed with RNA or metabolite extractions after desired treatment time.
Rapidly dab treated roots dry on sterilized paper towel and harvest directly into microcentrifuge tube.
Seal the top of the tube using parafilm, make two small holes, and submerge in liquid nitrogen.
Lyophilize samples for 3 days and store at -80 °C.
Select HRs that are white.
